# The Hook Bank — Patterns by Awareness Level

Built 2026-08-19 from TrendTrack study of Alevia (~25 long-forms incl. the new kidney batch), Eden Labs (main page + "Natural Healing with Dawn Miller" whitelist page), and Elvera (tryelvera.com). Companion to `_engine/swipe-library/long-form-copy/alevia-amla-system/ALEVIA-STUDY.md` and the copy-engine skill's awareness dial.

**Companion file:** [`VIDEO-HOOK-BANK.md`](VIDEO-HOOK-BANK.md) — the VIDEO ad hook skeletons (18 patterns from Nuora, Lymphoria, Sculptique, Resilia, PiPi Tea, Serene Herbs, built 2026-08-20). This file governs written copy hooks; that one governs spoken/visual openers. The governing law below applies to both.

## The governing law of hooks (Brooks, 2026-08-19)

**The hook calls out the CONCEPT, not the problem.** At unaware, the hook drops the reader into the situation that the angle will later explain. The reader recognizes themselves in the SCENE or the EMOTION long before any problem is named. The self-ID timing is the awareness dial in miniature:

- **Unaware**: self-ID happens through situation + unadmitted emotion (identity loss they won't admit). Problem never named in the hook.
- **Problem aware**: self-ID happens in line 1-2 through the felt symptom or the dismissed-by-doctor moment.
- **Solution aware**: self-ID happens IMMEDIATELY through the failed solution itself (the thing they're currently doing that isn't working).
- **Product aware**: self-ID through the product category + a pattern interrupt about it (negative hooks).
- **Most aware**: offer pattern interrupt.

**The congruence contract**: the hook is a check the body must cash. Every image in the hook (the jar, the peas, the index card, the good days) must return in the body as a closed loop, and the emotion the hook voices must be the same emotion the close resolves. Alevia's hooks are never generic curiosity; they are the story's most loaded scene, promoted.

**Hook jobs checklist (every hook, all levels)**: pattern interrupt that challenges a belief · emotional payoff promised · self-ID present or clearly incoming · and/or new mechanism teased.

---

## UNAWARE HOOKS (story-led long-forms, native feel, zero clinical language)

### U1 — The Paradox of Coping ("the good days lie")
Voices the avatar's private coping behavior or self-deception, the thing they do but have never said out loud.
> "I had a stretch of three good days in a row last spring and I almost forgot what was wrong with me. That's the part nobody warns you about. Not the bad days. The good ones. Because the good ones lie to you." (Alevia BP / Maureen, scaled + translated to French)
Why it works: instant caught-red-handed identification; challenges the belief "good days mean I'm getting better"; identity loss named without naming any problem.
Use when: the avatar oscillates between hope and symptoms and uses good days as an excuse not to act.

### U2 — The Stranger's Grief (witnessed mortality)
Narrator drops mid-situation into someone ELSE's tragedy; sadness hooks, death theme forecast, zero problem naming.
> "I helped a stranger load groceries into his trunk at the Walmart on East 71st last Tuesday and he ended up crying into a bag of frozen peas in front of me. I didn't know what to do." (Alevia cholesterol, RUNNING NOW, fresh duplicates)
Why it works: hyper-specific location = truth signal; "I didn't know what to do" = helplessness every reader shares; the tragedy belongs to a stranger so the reader's defenses stay down while the stakes soak in. Buyer-for-other engine (she buys for her husband).
Use when: mortality is the driver but the avatar would bounce off their own death being invoked directly.

### U3 — The Grief Relic (artifact hook)
A hyper-specific object carrying a dead loved one's presence; the health problem hides inside the object's meaning.
> "I found a jar of my mother's bread and butter pickles in the back of my pantry last Tuesday. She made them the summer before she died. 2021. The lid still had her handwriting on it in black Sharpie, 'JUNE, sweet' in that loopy way she wrote everything, like she was always halfway through a thought." (Alevia arthritis)
Why it works: "halfway through a thought" opens a curiosity loop; the jar is EXACTLY the object the arthritic avatar struggles with, so self-ID arrives through the hands without arthritis being named; whitelist page ("arthritis support community") pre-frames belonging.
Use when: the symptom lives in a daily object (jars, stairs, zippers, pens, registers).

### U4 — The Witnessed Tear (proxy identity loss)
A loved one crying over a mundane object; the narrator decodes the real reason.
> "My father wrote his chili recipe on an index card in 1981 and I found him crying over it last fall. He wasn't crying about the recipe. He was crying because he couldn't open the cumin jar." (Alevia neuropathy/joints, RUNNING 44 days)
Why it works: the correction structure ("He wasn't crying about X. He was crying because Y") is a mini belief-shift performed inside the hook; identity loss (the chili was his THING for 44 years) drives it; observer voice recruits adult children as buyers.
Use when: buyer-for-other lane; the sufferer's pride blocks direct address.

### U5 — The Accusation Bookend (results smuggled as scandal)
The strongest proof beat moved into line 1, disguised as an accusation or scandal, then re-earned all ad long.
> "My orthopedic surgeon asked me point blank if I'd been going to another clinic behind his back. I'm 56. He thought I was getting black market stem cell injections." (Alevia joints, their MOST duplicated ad, 12 copies)
Why it works: deniable bragging; borrows the credibility of the expensive miracle treatment; doctor astonishment as the opening frame.
Use when: you have a result so strong it needs a costume to be believable.

### U6 — The Forbidden Thought / Confession
The narrator confesses the thing the avatar has thought but would never say.
> "I burned my grandson's hand on a Saturday morning in February and I have not told anyone the truth about how it happened until right now." (Alevia joints)
> "I found a notebook in my husband's truck last March and I haven't told him I saw it." (Alevia neuropathy observer, longest-lived ad, 84+ days)
> "I was making my Christmas card list... and realized I'd crossed off 4 names this year... I looked at my husband eating his Cheerios and thought: you're going to be next." (Alevia BP wife)
Why it works: confession buys instant intimacy and truth-credit; the secret IS the curiosity loop; for observers, the complicity confession ("I had to pretend I didn't see it") voices universal caregiver behavior.
Use when: shame or secrecy is the avatar's actual daily texture.

### U7 — The Crisis Artifact (mundane object carrying death)
A bureaucratic or domestic object arrives carrying mortality.
> "The Christmas card I mailed to my cousin Patty in November came back to my house in February with a yellow sticker on it that said DECEASED." (Alevia cholesterol)
> "Got my lab results back today. LDL 216... Whatever that means." (Alevia cholesterol, lab-printout mirror)
Use when: the avatar's denial is paper-shaped (unread lab printouts, ignored letters, drawer artifacts).

### U8 — The Blue-Zone Traveler (borrowed-world curiosity)
Exotic longevity witness + a practice "Americans have completely forgotten."
> "My 97-year-old host in Sardinia, Italy eats cheese every morning, drinks red wine every night, has never taken a supplement, and hasn't seen a doctor in over 20 years. When I asked..." (Eden Labs whitelist)
> "There's a tiny Greek island called Ikaria where people literally forget to die." (Eden Labs whitelist)
Why it works: curiosity + aspiration instead of pain; zero threat, high share-ability; mechanism teased as ancient secret.
Use when: statics for cold unaware traffic where pain-first would get scroll-passed; works for gut/longevity products.

### U9 — The Villain Speaks (POV inversion)
The problem introduces itself in first person.
> "Hi. We're your parasites. And we've been living rent-free inside your gut for years. We built these walls so your immune system can't see us." (Eden Labs whitelist)
Why it works: maximal pattern interrupt; personifies the enemy so the mechanism becomes a character; self-ID via symptoms the "villain" brags about causing.
Use when: statics; the mechanism has a hideable culprit. (Check house personification laws per brand before using.)

### U10 — The Revenge Story (vindication engine)
Wronged-then-vindicated arc teased in 3 sentences; health payload arrives inside the story.
> "Excluded from my son's wedding in Sardinia, I went on vacation alone. When the wedding fell apart, my whole family frantically tried to reach me. I did not pick up the phone." (Eden Labs whitelist, run in multiple variants)
Why it works: pure drama loop, the health product enters as the source of her unbotheredness; dignity restoration is the buried promise for 55+ women.
Use when: unaware statics for avatars whose deep frame is being dismissed/managed by family.

### U11 — The Insider Witness (credentialed dread)
A professional who has watched the worst outcome for years, now facing or revealing it.
> "For 12 years, I walked into a dialysis room every morning. I know the chairs. I know the schedule. I know the exact sound..." (Alevia kidney, new batch)
> "I'm a parasitologist. I've spent 12 years studying parasites that live inside the human body." (Eden Labs whitelist, run in EN + ES)
> "'I told them it was a small procedure.' I've said a version of that sentence for eleven years." (Alevia kidney)
Why it works: authority transfer + the insider's secret; dread by proximity.
Use when: the category's nightmare endpoint (dialysis, amputation, surgery) is known to the avatar but abstract.

## PROBLEM-AWARE HOOKS (self-ID immediate; symptom or dismissal named in line 1)

### P1 — The NOT-Stack (belief inversion callout)
Attacks the avatar's current best guesses in a rhythmic triple, then teases the real mechanism.
> "Protecting your kidneys is NOT drinking more water. It is NOT cutting your protein down again. And it is definitely NOT..." (Alevia kidney, THE current heavy-duplication control)
Why it works: self-ID through behaviors only the diagnosed do; each NOT is a micro belief-shift; sets up the mechanism as the withheld answer.
Use when: the avatar is actively managing the problem with folk protocols.

### P2 — The Dismissal Mirror
Quotes the system's dismissal verbatim, then sides with the reader against it.
> Pattern (Alevia body copy promoted to hook position in several ads): "He said, 'A lot of women your age. Let's keep watching.'"
Use when: VoC shows the avatar's top wound is being waved off ("normal at your age," "borderline," "let's monitor").

### P3 — The Shock Scene (nightmare state, in medias res)
The problem's worst-case morning, timestamped.
> "It was 7:15 AM when I found my 72-year-old husband collapsed on our bathroom floor, clutching his stomach, tears streaming down his face, defeated by constipation that had stolen his independence." (Elvera, 1 of only 2 creatives they run)
Why it works: timestamp + posture + named emotion = cinematic truth; the stakes (independence) named in the first sentence; observer voice recruits spouses.
Use when: problem-aware audiences numb to symptom lists but not to consequences.

### P4 — The Symptom No-Matter-What
Names the symptom plus the avatar's full effort resume in one line.
> "If you're still constipated no matter how much fiber you eat, water you drink, or Miralax you take, your bacterial signal system is broken." (Elvera's mechanism static)
Why it works: "no matter how much" absorbs every objection in advance; instant mechanism handoff ("your signal system is broken") = problem reframed in line 1.
Use when: retargeting or problem-aware cold where the avatar has already tried the obvious. NOTE for Motilli: transpose to the NERVE signal mechanism (house law: signal = nerve, never bacteria).

### P5 — The If-Then Ladder
Stacked "If [your exact morning]" lines, each one a self-ID checkbox, resolving to one instruction.
> "If your stomach bloats after every meal no matter what you eat, use a castor oil pack. If you sleep nine hours and still wake up exhausted, use a castor oil pack." (Eden Labs)
Use when: statics; three symptoms that co-occur in the avatar.

## SOLUTION-AWARE HOOKS (self-ID through the FAILED SOLUTION, immediately)

### S1 — The Failed-Solution Confession (spend/escalation shame)
Self-ID through the exact failing remedy plus a private escalation the avatar hides.
> "I've now spent more on enema kits than I have on my actual Mounjaro prescription. And they stop working after the third one. I need to say that out loud because I haven't said it to anyone." (Motilli, our own; validated by this study as the correct S-level hook)
Why it works: the spend comparison is a pattern interrupt AND self-ID; "they stop working" challenges the belief the current fix is handling it; confession intimacy.
Use when: the avatar is mid-escalation on a failing solution (Miralax→enemas; fiber→laxatives).

### S2 — The Quitter Wins (social-comparison inversion)
The disciplined user loses to someone who stopped trying.
> "My blood pressure was 146/92 after two years of beetroot, garlic, magnesium, and fish oil. My sister's was 118/76 and she'd stopped taking all of it." (Alevia)
Why it works: weaponizes the avatar's own dashboard numbers; explodes the "just add more" belief; opens the mechanism loop (what does she know?).

### S3 — The Refusal (defiance of the standard escalation)
> "I refused cortisone shots for 3 years. Here's what happened to my joint pain. And by the end of this, you're gonna be pissed." (Alevia)
Why it works: refusing the gold standard is either brave or reckless, reader must find out which; recruits anger as fuel.
Use when: the next step on the avatar's conveyor belt is one they dread.

### S4 — The Treatment Is the Thief
The prescribed solution named as the destroyer, via a loved one's decline.
> "I've watched 2 blood pressure medications destroy my mother. Now my doctor wants to put me on the same ones. I'm a nurse." (Alevia, duplicated 6x in nerve variant)
> "22 months on Lisinopril... My doctor says we're 'managing the blood pressure well.' My husband says I forget things he told me an hour ago. One of them is lying." (Alevia)
COMPLIANCE RAIL: attack the paradigm (masks the number, nobody fixed the wall), never the drug's safety. Alevia's one same-day ad kill was direct statin disparagement.

## PRODUCT-AWARE / MOST-AWARE HOOKS (statics + offer ads; Eden Labs main page playbook)

### M1 — The Negative Review Fake-Out
> "DO NOT buy a castor oil pack. I don't want anyone making the same mistake I did. I wore one every night for two months. Nothing happened." (resolves: she bought a cheap knockoff; Eden's is different) (Eden Labs, duplicated)
> "I regret buying the Eden Labs castor oil pack." (resolves into praise + offer)
> "Unfortunately, I'll be returning my Eden Labs castor oil pack, but not for the reason you might think." (resolves: buying a second as a gift, etc.)
Why it works: negative sentiment is unclickbait-able for owners/considerers; resolves into moat (their version vs cheap versions) + offer. This is Alevia's "I need to publicly apologize... because I lied" pattern, same family.

### M2 — The Comment Reply (fake social listening)
> "'Love Eden Labs, but it's so expensive. Can you guys lower the price?' Okay, I'm about to blow your mind right now." (Eden Labs)
Why it works: the price objection is handled inside a conversation the reader feels they're overhearing; offer arrives as a favor.

### M3 — The Timeline Demo
> "This is what happens to your body when you wear a castor oil pack overnight for 30 days. After 24 hours..." (Eden Labs)
Why it works: future pacing as content; day-by-day structure mirrors the damaging-admission timeline inside one static.

### M4 — The Moat Spec ("what makes X different")
> "What makes Eden's castor oil different? Hexane free — most castor oil on Amazon..." (Eden Labs)
Use when: product-aware traffic comparison shopping; equivalent to Alevia's "not all Amla is Amla" block as a standalone ad.

## CLOSES (paired decision, 2026-08-19)

Brooks's law for our cold natives: **soft closes only. We have been selling too hard on Motilli natives; the story does the selling, the CTA whispers.**
- Preferred: the **edit-style close**: the story ends on the emotional beat with no pitch, then a casual afterthought carries the link. Pattern: "Edit: a few people asked, so adding it here. The gummies are called [X]. That's the link. That's all I've got." or "I realized I never left the link. It's [X]. Take it or leave it."
- Alevia's binary close ("You can keep treating the bottom... Or you can fix the part that's actually broken") stays in the bank for solution-aware, but the CTA that follows it should still be soft for our natives.
- Eden/Alevia hard stacks (scarcity + deal) are reserved for most-aware offer ads only.

## Swipe hygiene rules (house laws applied to this bank)

1. NEVER copy competitor proof numbers (Elvera's "1000-fold," "62% increase," "Patricia" are unverifiable/likely fabricated; our house law bans invented stats, studies, and named doctors).
2. Motilli mechanism transposition: any "signal" hook maps to the NERVE signal / top-not-bottom canonical mechanism, never bacteria.
3. Hook must be congruent with the concept: if the hook's scene/object doesn't appear again as a closed loop in the body, the hook is rejected.
4. Whitelist-page trick: run condition-community page names ("...Support Community", "Natural Healing with...") so the hook lands inside a context of belonging. Alevia (arthritis page) and Eden Labs (Dawn Miller page) both do this.
5. AI-tell laws apply to all hooks AND bodies (no em dashes, no "not X. It's Y." constructions in OUR copy). The ban covers the WHOLE pattern family, not just the literal form (caught by Brooks 2026-08-20): negation stacks ("Not a shout. Not a crash. The sound..."), correction reveals ("Not the sentence. The foil."), didn't-X-she-Y-because contrasts ("She didn't find him because of a crash. She found him because..."), trailing negation fragments ("Not since the mower." / "Not once."), and was-not-X-it-was-Y reveals. Sweep regex for audits: `(^|[.!?] )Not [a-z]+\. Not |(^|[.!?] )No [a-z]+\. No |Not once|Not since|It's not|That's not|isn't [a-z]+\. It's|wasn't [a-z]+\. It was|didn't [a-z ]+\. (She|He|I|It) [a-z]+ because`. Dialogue questions ("How did you know?") and single natural negations inside a sentence are fine.

6. **PARALLEL REPETITION STACKS are a separate ban (Brooks, 2026-08-21).** Anaphora (3+ consecutive sentences opening with the same word: "He quit... He ran... He did... He had..."), same-word tricolons ("Same laugh, same stubborn hair, same blood"), and balanced fragment triples ("Tomatoes by the grocery bag. A morning walk with Dot. Third row at every graduation."). **The test: is the CONTENT genuinely parallel, or is the parallel decoration?** A chronological ladder (At 43 / At 45 / At 47), a recited list of family deaths (father at 58, his father at 56), a results timeline (Week one, nothing. Week two, nothing.), and an enumerated moat (one line / two lines / all three) all EARN it, because the world is actually shaped that way. Character traits, life sketches, and emotional payoffs do NOT, and those are exactly where the reaching happens.

   **Diagnostic worth remembering:** every violation in the Lunessa mower draft clustered at the emotional peaks (the reveal, the funeral meaning, the aunt's life, the daughter payoff, the close). AI reaches for symmetry when it's trying to land a beat, because balance *feels* like emphasis. Real writers get plainer and more specific under emotion, not more balanced. When a paragraph is the most important one in the piece, check it hardest.

8. **NO PERSONIFICATION OF ABSTRACTIONS (Brooks, 2026-08-21, banner law).** An emotion, a span of time, a number, or any other abstraction cannot occupy space, move on its own, or take an action. "Grief was in there." "Eleven years reorganized themselves in front of me." "Fear sat down next to me." All banned. The fix is almost never a rephrase, it's a CUT: name the concrete act instead and let the reader infer the feeling, per [[feedback-ugc-demonstrate-never-describe]]. Allowed: dead idioms where nobody reads agency ("water finding its level"), standard metric usage ("the number climbs," "prices rise"), machines doing what machines do ("the mower chewing a hole in the grass"), and explicitly-flagged magical thinking the narrator is confessing ("as if the blood could hear me being good"). Sweep regex: `(grief|years|number|time|fear|silence|memory|guilt|hope|the past) (was|were|sat|stood|came|walked|reached|held|found|told|knew|decided|wanted|reorganiz)`.

7. **Stating the obvious is its own AI tell.** "Danny and I came from the same two people" (siblings share parents). "She is not inheriting the countdown. That stops with me" (same idea twice). Cut any sentence whose only job is to explain a relationship the reader already inferred, and never say a thing twice in different words for rhythm.

   Detector for both, run on every draft: split the body into paragraphs, split those into sentences, flag any run of 3+ sentences sharing a first word, plus any pair of short sentences sharing a first word. Read each hit and ask the decoration question before cutting.
